text:
Anders Lee left the Islanders after 923 games and eight seasons as captain, signing a three-year deal with Utah on July 1, and at 36 he's doing what he has always done: going to the net. With him on the ice at five on five, the Mammoth take 63% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, almost nine points better than when he sits.

The goals have lagged. He has three on 6.0 expected goals, an 8.8% shooting rate, and one goal in his last ten games. That's the kind of gap that usually closes for a net-front player, because the chances keep coming from the same place. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 91st percentile for scoring chances from the home-plate area last season.

The reasonable worry is age. He's playing under 14 minutes a night, mostly at even strength, and the power-play time is thin (one point). But the process looks like the Lee who scored 20 goals eight times in ten seasons.
headline: Lee is getting the looks in Utah
